literal: Disgrace-causing unpleasant things even if does, to the intoxicated toddy-like indeed, O thief, your chest.
translation: O thief! Your chest is exactly like toddy to those addicted to it: they desire it even if it causes them disgraceful sorrow.
modern: கள்வா! இழிவான துன்பங்களைச் செய்தாலும், குடித்தவர்களுக்குக் கள் எப்படி விருப்பமானதாக இருக்குமோ, அதுபோலவே உன் மார்பு எனக்கு இருக்கிறது.
explanation: The speaker addresses her lover as a 'thief' (கள்வ) because he has stolen her heart and caused her distress by his absence. She compares his chest to toddy (கள்). Toddy brings public disgrace and misery (இளித்தக்க இன்னா) to those who consume it, yet those who are intoxicated by it (களித்தார்க்கு) cannot stay away. In the exact same way, even though her lover's actions have caused her shameful suffering, she remains intoxicated by his love and eagerly desires his embrace.
